question: Of the patients with an normal level of IGG, how many of them admitted to the hospital?
evidence: normal level of IGG refers to 900 < IGG < 2000; admitted to the hospital refers to Admission = '+';
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.IGG > 900 AND T2.IGG < 2000 AND T1.Admission = '+'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.IGG > 900 AND T2.IGG <2000 AND  T1.Admission = '+'

b.request: How many distinct patients (counting each ID once) have a laboratory IGG value strictly between 900 and 2000 and a Patient Admission value of '+'?
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient AS P INNER JOIN Laboratory AS L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.IGG > 900 AND L.IGG < 2000 AND P.Admission = '+'
b.raw: How many distinct patients (counting each ID once) have a laboratory IGG value strictly between 900 and 2000 and a Patient Admission value of '+'?

d.request: Of the patients with a normal IGG level (900 < IGG < 2000), how many were admitted to the hospital (Admission = '+'), counting each distinct patient ID only once?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.IGG > 900 AND L.IGG < 2000 AND P.Admission = '+'
